web.title: Log evaluation data from your code - Weights & Biases Documentation
web.description:
## Documentation Index
This guide shows you how to use `EvaluationLogger` to record predictions and scores from your existing Python or TypeScript code, so you can evaluate model performance in Weave without first defining a full dataset and scorer suite. Use this approach when your dataset or scorers aren’t defined upfront, or when you need to log evaluation data incrementally as your workflow runs.In contrast to the standard `Evaluation` object, which requires a predefined `Dataset` and list of `Scorer` objects, the `EvaluationLogger` lets you log individual predictions and their associated scores incrementally as they become available.

## [​](https://docs.wandb.ai/weave/guides/evaluation/evaluation_logger#basic-workflow)  Basic workflow
2. _Log predictions:_ Call `log_prediction()` for each input and output pair from your system.

## [​](https://docs.wandb.ai/weave/guides/evaluation/evaluation_logger#basic-example)  Basic example
- The input and output are logged using `log_prediction`.

## [​](https://docs.wandb.ai/weave/guides/evaluation/evaluation_logger#simplified-logging-with-log_example)  Simplified logging with `log_example()`
```
prediction = eval_logger.log_prediction(inputs=inputs, output=output)
prediction.log_score(scorer="correctness", score=output == sample['expected'])
prediction.finish()
```

## [​](https://docs.wandb.ai/weave/guides/evaluation/evaluation_logger#advanced-usage)  Advanced usage
### [​](https://docs.wandb.ai/weave/guides/evaluation/evaluation_logger#log-and-compare-multiple-evaluations)  Log and compare multiple evaluations
```
import weave

models = [\
    "model1",\
    "model2",\
     {"name": "model3", "metadata": {"coolness": 9001}}\
]

for model in models:
    # EvalLogger must be initialized before model calls to capture tokens
    ev = EvaluationLogger(
        name="comparison-eval",
        model=model,
        dataset="example_dataset",
        scorers=["greater_than_3_scorer", "greater_than_5_scorer", "greater_than_7_scorer"],
        eval_attributes={"experiment_id": "exp_123"}
    )
    for inputs in your_dataset:
        output = your_output_generator(**inputs)
        prediction = ev.log_prediction(inputs=inputs, output=output)
        prediction.log_score(scorer="greater_than_3_scorer", score=output > 3)
        prediction.log_score(scorer="greater_than_5_scorer", score=output > 5)
        prediction.log_score(scorer="greater_than_7_scorer", score=output > 7)
        prediction.finish()

    ev.log_summary()
```

web.title: Weights & Biases: Learn LLMs the “Instrument-Everything” Way
web.description:
# Weights & Biases: Learn LLMs the “Instrument-Everything” Way
## Evaluate What Matters: quality, cost, and latency (with Weave)
### A small, repeatable evaluation (Python)
Below we use **Weave’s EvaluationLogger** to log predictions **incrementally** (handy for complex apps or streaming).

```
# pip install weave openai
import time, math, weave
from openai import OpenAI
from weave import EvaluationLogger

weave.init("llm-learn-101")                # project name
client = OpenAI()                          # needs OPENAI_API_KEY

# 1) Tiny eval set (make this YOUR use case)
eval_rows = [\
    {"id": 1, "question": "What are our support hours?", "expected": "9am–5pm"},\
    {"id": 2, "question": "How to reset my password?",   "expected": "Use the reset link"},\
    {"id": 3, "question": "Where to contact billing?",   "expected": "billing@example.com"},\
]

# Prices (USD per 1K tokens). Replace with your provider/prices.
PRICE_IN  = 0.005
PRICE_OUT = 0.015

def estimate_cost_cents(prompt_toks: int, completion_toks: int) -> float:
    usd = (prompt_toks/1000.0)*PRICE_IN + (completion_toks/1000.0)*PRICE_OUT
    return round(usd*100, 4)

# 2) Start an incremental evaluation
eval_logger = EvaluationLogger(model="gpt-4o", dataset="faq-mini")  # flexible labels

correct = 0
total_cost_cents = 0.0

for row in eval_rows:
    t0 = time.time()

    # Model call (Weave patches OpenAI calls to track tokens/latency in traces)
    resp = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="gpt-4o",
        messages=[\
            {"role":"system", "content":"Answer briefly and factually."},\
            {"role":"user", "content": row["question"]},\
        ],
        temperature=0.0,
        max_tokens=50,
    )
    pred = resp.choices[0].message.content.strip()
    usage = resp.usage or type("u", (), {"prompt_tokens":0, "completion_tokens":0})  # safety
    latency_ms = (time.time() - t0) * 1000

    # 3) Log the prediction (inputs/outputs) to Weave
    p = eval_logger.log_prediction(inputs=row, output={"pred": pred})

    # 4) Compute and log scores
    exact = int(pred.lower() == row["expected"].lower())
    contains = int(row["expected"].lower() in pred.lower())
    cost_cents = estimate_cost_cents(usage.prompt_tokens, usage.completion_tokens)

    eval_logger.log_score(p, name="exact_match",   value=exact)
    eval_logger.log_score(p, name="contains_rule", value=contains)
    eval_logger.log_score(p, name="latency_ms",    value=latency_ms)
    eval_logger.log_score(p, name="cost_cents",    value=cost_cents)

    eval_logger.finish(p)

    correct += exact
    total_cost_cents += cost_cents

# 5) Aggregate and log a summary (e.g., cost per correct)
summary = {
    "accuracy": correct / len(eval_rows),
    "total_cost_cents": total_cost_cents,
    "cost_per_correct_cents": (total_cost_cents / max(correct, 1)),
}
eval_logger.log_summary(summary)
print("Summary:", summary)
```
